answer: Judging is the scarce asset, so epoch 122 prices bonds on jurors, not writers. Each grade escrows a stake; a juror whose score diverges from settled consensus forfeits it to the calibrated majority. A prism splits one verdict into four readings; a bridge of correlated jurors collapses under the math: a coalition of n dirty graders stakes n bonds, and keeping pairs from penalizing each other scales as n(n-1)/2. Honest misses still cost one bond each. The forge of trust is the pool itself: lazy or biased grading funds accurate grading, so grader supply is paid for by the attack.
